statuses.title: Enforce stop-at-epsilon on every accounted step
statuses.note: Per-step enforcement is real for deterministic accountants: predict_stop_step (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:272) binary-searches the crossing step at setup and the loop checks 'global_step >= ctx.stop_at_step' after every accounted step (:1874), placed after 'ctx.accounting |= ctx.step_process' (:1766) and the log/save/eval gate; resume short-circuits when the restored accountant already exceeds target (:1139-1161). Unit tests (TestPredictStopStep) and cadence-independence tests pass (ran locally: 5 passed). CAVEAT: Monte-Carlo accountants (sampling_mode b_min_sep / balls_in_bins, the canonical samplers for mf_band/mf_blt/mf_bisr/mf_bsr/mf_lambda_cgd) are excluded at :1175 and keep the pre-fix log-boundary-only check (:3970), which never fires with logging disabled — see finding. Second caveat: k_out_of_t's flat prefix epsilon makes the predicted stop step k0+1 — see finding.

statuses.title: Honor fractional num_train_epochs
statuses.note: _steps_breakdown (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trainer/_dp_trainer.py:4474) now computes total = ceil(num_train_epochs * steps_per_epoch) and num_epochs = ceil(num_train_epochs); the inner loop's total_steps ceiling (:1895) cuts the partial final epoch, the sampler is built with n_steps=total_steps, and calibration/accounting/scheduler all consume the same total. Tests assert step count, privacy_total_steps, reference epsilon at the fractional horizon, LR schedule values, and the 0<f<1 one-step case.

statuses.title: Evaluate SFT DFT runs with the training objective
statuses.note: SFTTrainer.prediction_step (packages/opaque-transformers/src/opaque/api/transformers/trl/_sft_trainer.py:563) routes loss_type='dft' through the vmapped per-example DFT eval closure in every mode including prediction_loss_only=True (the best-model path), and _eval_token_weighted_loss=False (:199) makes eval_loss the plain per-example mean instead of a realized-token-count reconstruction (base aggregation branch at _dp_trainer.py:2754-2780). nll/chunked_nll keep the inherited CE path. Numerical tests compare eval_loss against an independently computed DFT reference (test_trl_trainers.py:1785-1903).

statuses.title: Align best-model selection with save and evaluation boundaries
statuses.note: Two-part fix confirmed in the current tree: (1) _maybe_log_save_evaluate forces ctrl.should_save=True when an eval improves the best metric under load_best_model_at_end, so the just-evaluated params are materialized at that step; (2) BestModelSaveCallback is auto-injected for load_best_model_at_end (not just save_strategy='best') in _dp_trainer.py:~505, and best_model_checkpoint is registered by folder lookup so rotation cannot delete it. __post_init__ validates strategy/step-multiple alignment (_training_arguments.py:603-655). Covered by test_checkpoint_correctness.py (best_metric_forces_checkpoint_at_intermediate_eval_step, best_eval_only_step_forces_checkpoint, best_folder_lookup).

statuses.title: Test the actual Hugging Face evaluation cadence

statuses.title: Gather uneven distributed evaluation shards safely
statuses.note: gather_tensors/gather_pytree (opaque-engine distributed/_state.py:290-313) use dist.all_gather_object on CPU payloads — object collectives carry variable sizes, so uneven shards cannot truncate or pad; _merge_gathered_pytrees validates dtype/ndim/non-concat dims and pytree structure and tolerates empty (None) rank shards. Eval loss totals are sum-reduced with exact scalar reduction, and cluster-wide num_samples avoids post-gather truncation to one shard (_dp_trainer.py:2860-2876). Exercised by the blocking Gloo lane (test_gloo_eval_gather_matches_reference_for_uneven_shards, test_gloo_eval_gather_supports_empty_rank_shard).

findings.title: Stop-at-epsilon still only fires at log boundaries for Monte-Carlo accountant modes
findings.claim: The #392 fix (commit b7073f37, closed issue 392 'Enforce stop-at-epsilon on every accounted step') deliberately excludes sampling_mode 'b_min_sep' and 'balls_in_bins' from the per-step predicted stop ('a.sampling_mode not in ("b_min_sep", "balls_in_bins")' at :1175); for those modes the only stop mechanism remains the fallback inside 'if ctrl.should_log:' in _maybe_log_save_evaluate (:3955-3983), i.e. the exact pre-fix log-boundary behavior the issue was filed about. These are the CANONICAL samplers for every DP-FTRL mechanism except mf_identity (_SAMPLER_BY_MECHANISM, _training_arguments.py:171-179).
findings.failure_scenario: User sets privacy_noise_mechanism='mf_blt' (auto sampling_mode='balls_in_bins'), a fixed privacy_noise_multiplier and privacy_target_epsilon, with default logging_steps=500: epsilon crosses the target at step 900 but training continues to step 1000 before the next log boundary checks — up to 499 extra accounted steps of privacy spend past the declared target. With logging_strategy='no' the stop NEVER fires and the run consumes the full horizon regardless of the target.
evidence: _dp_trainer.py:1171-1176: 'and a.sampling_mode not in ("b_min_sep", "balls_in_bins")' gates predict_stop_step
_dp_trainer.py:3955 'if ctrl.should_log:' ... :3969-3977 fallback stop only when 'ctx.stop_at_step is None'
_training_arguments.py:171-179: b_min_sep/balls_in_bins are the auto samplers for mf_band/mf_blt/mf_bisr/mf_bsr/mf_lambda_cgd
docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:76-79 documents 'logging_steps=0 disables it silently'
findings.fix_sketch: For MC accountants, either evaluate epsilon_at on every accounted step (amortized via acc.cached), or refuse/warn loudly at setup when privacy_target_epsilon is combined with a Monte-Carlo sampling mode and a non-per-step logging cadence, so the user knows the target is enforced only at log boundaries.

findings.title: predict_stop_step halts k_out_of_t runs after one accounted step (flat prefix epsilon)
findings.claim: KOutOfT.pld_at with total_participations > 1 'snaps to the full-horizon bound' for every prefix (packages/opaque-dpsgd/src/opaque/api/accounting/dpsgd/amplification/_k_out_of_t.py:28-33), so epsilon(K) is constant in K — verified numerically: (per_step(k_out_of_t(gaussian(1.0), total_participations=4, n_steps=100)) * K).epsilon_at(1e-5) == 2.4083 for K in {1,2,5,50,100}. predict_stop_step's binary search then returns k0+1 whenever target <= horizon epsilon, and its boundary guard (eps(lo)>=target, lo==1 so no lo-1 probe) accepts it, so the trainer stops after ONE accounted step.
findings.failure_scenario: sampling_mode='k_out_of_t' + fixed privacy_noise_multiplier + privacy_target_epsilon at or below the full-horizon epsilon: train() performs a single optimizer step, sets privacy_target_epsilon_reached=True, and returns what looks like a successful run with an essentially untrained model. Pre-#392 the same config trained until the first log boundary (default 500 steps); the fix silently changed this to 1 step. The setup log line ('will stop after step 1 of N') is the only signal.
evidence: _k_out_of_t.py:28-33: 'Prefix accounting ... with total_participations > 1 snaps to the full-horizon bound'
Numerical check in this session: epsilon flat at 2.4083134058043343 for K=1..100
_dp_trainer.py:305-320 (binary search + boundary guard passes on a constant sequence with lo=1)
findings.fix_sketch: In predict_stop_step, treat eps(1) >= target as a degenerate prediction: warn explicitly that the accountant reports the full-horizon bound from step 1 for this sampling mode and either refuse the fixed-NM+target combination for k_out_of_t or fall back to no stop with a loud warning telling the user to calibrate against the horizon instead.

findings.title: wpo_weights omits the WPO Eq.(2) weight-alignment term that TRL and the paper apply
findings.claim: wpo_weights computes exp(mean masked per-token logp) only, while WPO Eq.(2) (arXiv:2406.11827) and TRL's use_weighting additionally subtract the per-token log-sum of squared token probabilities (verified in installed trl 1.12.0 DPOTrainer source: 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper ... lse1 = logsumexp(shift_logits); lse2 = logsumexp(2*shift_logits); log_denom = lse2 - 2*lse1 ...'). The module docstring (:3-22) and docs/alignment/trainers.md:283-285 present the shipped weighting as the paper's method without caveat. The divergence was exposed by the #380/#431 parity work and xfail'ed (packages/opaque-alignment/tests/test_trl_parity.py:518, reason: 'wpo_weights omits the WPO weight-alignment term log(sum_v p_v^2)') instead of fixed or documented user-facing.
findings.failure_scenario: A user migrating a TRL DPO run with use_weighting=True gets systematically different per-example weights (opaque's weights over-weight high-entropy completions relative to WPO's), so training dynamics and results silently diverge from both TRL and the cited paper while the docs claim equivalence. Utility only — the weight is detached and per-example, so per-example DP is unaffected. May be nominally in scope of open umbrella issues #323/#475, but neither names this concrete divergence, which was discovered after they were filed.
evidence: _wpo.py:33-46: returns (masked logp sum / count).detach().exp() with no alignment term
trl 1.12.0 DPOTrainer (inspected in-session): computes lse2 - 2*lse1 correction under 'Eq (2) of the WPO paper'
test_trl_parity.py:518 xfail reason text; pytest run: 1 xfailed
docs/alignment/trainers.md:283-285 documents use_weighting as arXiv:2406.11827 without caveat
findings.fix_sketch: Either extend wpo_weights to accept the logits (or the precomputed per-token log-denominator) and apply Eq.(2)'s log(sum_v p_v^2) term, or document in _wpo.py and docs/alignment/trainers.md that opaque implements the simplified sequence-probability weight and differs from TRL/the paper.

findings.title: Stop-at-epsilon user guide still documents the pre-#392 log-boundary-only behavior
findings.claim: The 'Stop-at-ε' section states 'training halts at the first logging boundary where the accumulated ε ... meets or exceeds the target' and 'The check runs every logging_steps (so setting logging_steps=0 disables it silently — explicit logging is the contract for stop-at-ε visibility)'. After commit b7073f37 this is false for every deterministic accountant: the check is a per-step integer comparison independent of logging cadence (test_stop_at_epsilon_independent_of_logging_cadence asserts exactly this), and it is accurate only for the b_min_sep/balls_in_bins Monte-Carlo modes. The in-source field comment (_training_arguments.py:479-481) repeats the stale claim.
findings.failure_scenario: A user reads that logging_steps=0 disables stop-at-epsilon and relies on that to run past the target while keeping the args set — on any deterministic accountant the run now stops at the predicted step anyway; conversely a b_min_sep user reads nothing telling them their mode is the one still on the weaker contract.
evidence: docs/user-guide/huggingface/training-arguments.md:72-79
_training_arguments.py:479-481 comment 'training halts at the first log boundary'
b7073f37 touched only _dp_trainer.py and tests — no doc update
validation/test_dp_trainer.py:256 test_stop_at_epsilon_independent_of_logging_cadence
findings.fix_sketch: Rewrite the section: deterministic accountants stop on the predicted accounted step regardless of logging cadence; b_min_sep/balls_in_bins fall back to the log-boundary check (and are disabled with logging off). Update the field comment to match.

findings.title: from_hf doc still claims adamw_torch_fused maps to optim_args={'fused': True}
findings.claim: The conversion doc lists 'adamw_torch_fused → adamw + optim_args={"fused": True}', but commit 6cc02681 (issue #389) changed _optim_collapse to return {'optim': 'adamw'} with a RuntimeWarning and no optim_args (_hf_convert.py:254-262), and the test asserts 'not opaque.optim_args'. The doc describes the removed behavior that used to raise TypeError at optimizer build.
findings.failure_scenario: A user reading the migration doc expects fused execution to be requested via optim_args after conversion and may hand-write optim_args={'fused': True} on optim='adamw' — which the opaque adamw factory rejects with TypeError on unknown keys — or simply mis-reports what their converted run does.

findings.fix_sketch: Change the bullet to 'adamw_torch_fused → adamw (RuntimeWarning: no fused kernel on the functional DP path)'.
